report.summary: Checkout-service and api-gateway error rates jumped at 09:00 UTC, well after the 08:54 checkout deploy, and both services began logging certificate failures for auth.internal within seconds of its stated notAfter of 08:59:59Z. The system determination is conclusive at confidence 0.75, with the leading hypothesis being expiry of the auth.internal serving certificate. Errors persisted through 09:30 with no contradicting evidence recorded. Served-certificate identity (subject, notAfter, fingerprint) was never retrieved, so the certificate-to-expiry link is supported by log text but not directly verified. The checkout deploy v2.15.1 is a weak lead, described as copy-only and not diffed. Sign-in and checkout failures share the auth.internal dependency rather than being independent faults.

root_cause.mechanism: The auth.internal serving certificate reached notAfter at 08:59:59Z, so TLS clients validating it fail from 09:00. checkout-service fails PKIX validity checks on auth.internal:8443 from 09:00:04Z and api-gateway fails x509 auth checks on cn=auth.internal from 09:00:15Z, producing the 09:00 error step in both services and the drop in auth request_rate to about 3 req/s.
assumptions: The certificate served on auth.internal:8443 is the one whose notAfter is 08:59:59Z, which is not directly verified
Client error text accurately names the cause
auth-service request_rate drop reflects clients failing TLS before reaching auth

ranked_hypotheses.mechanism: Clock skew or a different served certificate on auth.internal:8443 causes PKIX validity failures starting at 09:00 without a true expiry, with the gateway error text misleading. Both clients would still fail in the same bucket.
assumptions: Client clocks or served certificate differ from what error text states
No clock-skew query was run

ranked_hypotheses.mechanism: The v2.15.1 deploy at 08:54:00Z changed certificate or trust-store validation in checkout so it rejects a valid auth.internal certificate. This would explain checkout errors, but not the api-gateway x509 expiry errors, and the six-minute gap before onset makes it less likely.
assumptions: The deploy diff contains more than its described static-string changes
api-gateway failures are a separate coincidence

api-gateway error_rate was about 0.37-0.47% through 08:45, then 11.66% at 09:00 and 10.5-11.76% through 09:30.
The first checkout-service error at 09:00:04Z reads PKIX path validation failed, validity check failed (peer auth.internal:8443).
The first api-gateway error at 09:00:15Z reads x509 certificate has expired, current time is after 2026-09-05T08:59:59Z (cn=auth.internal).
api-gateway logged 20 expiry errors from 09:00:15Z to 09:30:00Z, and checkout-service ERROR lines continue through 09:30:00Z.

inferred_conclusions.statement: The leading cause is expiry of the auth.internal serving certificate at 08:59:59Z, which causes TLS validation failures in checkout-service and api-gateway from 09:00 onward; this is the system's conclusive determination.
The 08:54 checkout deploy is unlikely to be the direct trigger, because error rates stayed normal for six minutes after it and the errors cite certificate expiry rather than a checkout code path.
Sign-in and checkout failures share one upstream cause at auth.internal rather than being two separate faults, given that both services fail on the same certificate within 11-15 seconds.
Clock skew or a different served certificate on auth.internal is a lower-probability alternative that the available evidence does not rule out.

remediation.action: Renew or replace the auth.internal serving certificate immediately and reload auth-service so it serves a valid certificate.
remediation.rationale: The expired certificate is the leading cause of the 33% checkout and 11% gateway error rates, and no other mitigation addresses it.

remediation.action: Verify the served certificate on auth.internal:8443 (subject, notAfter, fingerprint) after renewal and confirm that checkout and api-gateway errors stop.
remediation.rationale: The certificate identity is unverified, and post-fix confirmation is the only check that settles it.

remediation.action: Hold further checkout-service rollouts until v2.15.1 is diffed for trust-store or TLS-validation changes.
remediation.rationale: The deploy is a weak lead and its code diff was never checked, so a rollback decision should rest on evidence.

remediation.action: Find out why cert-manager did not renew auth.internal before 08:59:59Z and fix that renewal path.
remediation.rationale: Renewal history was not retrieved, so the failure mode behind the missed renewal is unknown.

remediation.action: Add certificate expiry alerting for auth.internal and other internal serving certificates with lead time before notAfter.
remediation.rationale: The incident was detected only after the certificate had already expired and 33% of checkout requests had failed.

remediation.action: Make the auth-service health check exercise the TLS serving path on 8443 and validate certificate validity.
remediation.rationale: The current plaintext /health check on 8080 reported healthy during a full outage.

remediation.action: Add auth-service logging for TLS handshake and certificate events so that rejected clients are visible on the server side.
remediation.rationale: auth-service logged nothing for the failure, which made the server-side view hard to confirm.

remediation.action: Run a fleet-wide certificate expiry audit and check payment-service for the same PKIX error, following the P06 pattern.
remediation.rationale: The payment-service check was not run, and P06 shows a similar expiry failure has happened before.

brief.title: sign-in and checkout failures
brief.alert: ALERT [P1] checkout-service error rate 33% since ~09:00 UTC; users cannot sign in or complete checkout. A checkout-service deploy went out at 08:54 UTC.

plan.incident_understanding: P1 incident: checkout-service error rate reached about 33% since roughly 09:00 UTC, with users unable to sign in or complete checkout. api-gateway is also alerting. A checkout-service deploy at 08:54 UTC immediately precedes onset, making it the leading suspect, but the sign-in failures suggest a shared dependency (auth, session store, or gateway) may be involved rather than the deploy alone.
candidate_explanations: Regression in the checkout-service deploy at 08:54 UTC causing errors in checkout paths, with sign-in failures from a shared path or gateway effect
A downstream dependency of checkout-service (payment, inventory, or auth/session store) degraded around 09:00 UTC, independent of the deploy
A config change or feature flag change in api-gateway or auth routing causing sign-in and checkout failures
Infrastructure event (capacity, network, or certificate issue) affecting api-gateway and its upstreams around 09:00 UTC

findings.summary: Error onset for both checkout-service and api-gateway is in the 09:00 UTC bucket, not at the 08:54 deploy. Error rates were at baseline through 08:55. The first auth-related errors are at 09:00:04 (checkout) and 09:00:15 (api-gateway), just after an auth.internal certificate expired at 08:59:59Z. Both services fail on the same certificate problem in auth.internal, so sign-in and checkout are failing together through a shared dependency, not separately. The 08:54 deploy is six minutes before onset and the logs show no deploy-related error. Log lines carry no endpoint or HTTP status fields, so per-endpoint and status-code breakdowns could not be confirmed.

observations.statement: checkout-service error_rate was flat at about 0.26–0.33% from 08:00 through the 08:55 bucket, then jumped to 33.91% at the 09:00 bucket (max at 09:00:00) and stayed between 30.77% and 32.85% through 09:30.
api-gateway error_rate was flat at about 0.34–0.47% through the 08:55 bucket, then rose to 11.66% at 09:00 and stayed between 10.5% and 11.76% through 09:30 (max 11.76% at 09:20).

checkout-service cpu_pct, memory_pct, latency_p99_ms and request_rate stayed in their normal ranges across 08:00–09:30 (cpu 39–43%, memory 56–60%, p99 307–332 ms, request rate 82–87 req/s), with no step change at 08:54 or 09:00.
api-gateway cpu_pct, memory_pct, latency_p99_ms and request_rate stayed normal across the window (cpu 37–39%, p99 173–186 ms, request rate 405–436 req/s), with no step change at 08:54 or 09:00.

The first checkout-service error signature in the 09:00 window is 'auth-service token validation failed: javax.net.ssl.SSLHandshakeException: PKIX path validation failed ... validity check failed (peer auth.internal:8443)' at 09:00:04Z. Roughly 45 of these appear across the window, and the 30 returned lines run from 09:00:04Z to 09:19:45Z.

The first api-gateway error at 09:00:15Z is 'auth check failed: x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid: current time is after 2026-09-05T08:59:59Z (cn=auth.internal)'. About 20 of these appear, repeating through 09:30:00Z.

The api-gateway log window shows no errors before 09:00:15Z apart from one client-closed 499 on /api/v1/products at 08:22:19Z and slow-upstream WARNs on /api/v1/search (up to 1336 ms at 08:11). These are background noise and do not match the 09:00 error step.
checkout-service logged a single 'order rejected: card declined by issuer' at 08:13:47Z, which is background noise and does not explain the step change.

The checkout error signatures and the api-gateway error signatures both reference auth.internal (auth-service on 8443 for checkout, cn=auth.internal for the gateway). The two services' failures begin 11–15 seconds apart and share the same expiry timestamp of 08:59:59Z.

interpretations.statement: The onset is caused by the expiry of the auth.internal TLS certificate at 08:59:59Z, which precedes the first errors by about 5–15 seconds. Both checkout and gateway auth validation fail on that certificate.

The 08:54 checkout deploy is unlikely to be the direct trigger. Error rates stayed normal for 6 minutes after the deploy, and the errors cite a certificate expiry rather than a code or config failure in checkout. The deploy has not been fully ruled out, since it could have changed how checkout validates certificates, and that needs checking.

Sign-in and checkout are not independent failures. Both route through auth-service, and the api-gateway auth check and checkout's token validation fail on the same certificate. The likely shared cause is the auth.internal certificate and not two separate faults.
The HTTP status codes 401/403/500/503 are not confirmed by the returned data. The gateway error_rate jump is consistent with the auth failures but does not show which codes were returned.

data_gaps: Log records contain no HTTP status code or endpoint/route field for the auth and checkout errors, so the status-code breakdown and sign-in vs checkout endpoint split could not be confirmed directly.

The auth-service request_rate drop at 09:00Z is likely because checkout and other clients fail TLS to auth.internal before reaching auth-service. The flat auth error_rate fits this: rejected handshakes may never reach auth's request handling and so may not be counted as auth errors.

Auth-service itself appears healthy by its own metrics and logs (flat CPU, latency, memory, error rate). This argues against an auth-side crash or overload, though it does not rule out a certificate problem that auth never logs.
